title: Understanding the Assignment and Choosing a Position

source_framework.name: IES Teaching Secondary Students to Write Effectively
source_framework.recommendation: Recommendation 1: Explicitly teach appropriate writing strategies using a Model-Practice-Reflect instructional cycle.
source_framework.use_in_this_lesson: Informs the sequence of a short model, supported practice, and reflection. It does not validate EssayScaff's NLP rules or this specific lesson's learning outcomes.

source_framework.name: Self-Regulated Strategy Development (SRSD)
source_framework.citation: Harris, K. R., & Graham, S. (2016). Self-Regulated Strategy Development in Writing: Policy Implications of an Evidence-Based Practice. Policy Insights from the Behavioral and Brain Sciences, 3(1), 77-84.
principles_used: Model the strategy with a worked example.
Give the learner supported practice and explanatory feedback.
Invite self-monitoring and reflection on the learner's own writing.
Let the learner return to independent writing without an automated quality judgment.

learning_objectives: Identify the subject an essay assignment asks you to think about.
Distinguish a topic description from a position that answers the assignment.
Explain how a clear Introduction direction helps readers follow the essay.

model.heading: Learn from an example
instruction: Read the assignment once to find its subject. Then ask what question or decision you are being asked to consider.
A topic names what the writing is about. A position answers the assignment with a point of view another reader could discuss or disagree with.
A reason tells readers why you hold that position. An Introduction gives readers a direction; your own wording and the number of sentences can vary.
Use these questions as a planning aid, not a required sentence formula.

teacher_authored_example.assignment: Should our school offer one outdoor lunch day each week?
teacher_authored_example.topic: A weekly outdoor lunch day at school.
teacher_authored_example.topic_explanation: This names the subject, but it does not answer whether the school should offer it.
teacher_authored_example.description_sentence: Outdoor lunch is a time when students eat outside.
teacher_authored_example.description_explanation: This explains the topic but does not take a position on the assignment question.
teacher_authored_example.position_sentence: Our school should offer one outdoor lunch day each week because it could give students a relaxing break and a chance to connect with classmates.
teacher_authored_example.position_explanation: This answers the question with a position and gives a reason the writer could explain in the Body.
teacher_authored_example.direction_explanation: A reader can tell what the writer thinks and what reason the essay may explain. The writer can still revise this position or choose a different one.

practice.heading: Try it yourself
practice.instructions: Choose an answer for each question. Read the explanation, then continue when your answer is correct. You can retry a question at any time.

questions.prompt: For the assignment “Should our school offer one outdoor lunch day each week?”, which choice names the topic rather than answering the question?

options.text: A weekly outdoor lunch day at school.
options.feedback: Correct. This names the subject of the assignment without saying what the school should do.

options.text: Our school should offer an outdoor lunch day each week.
options.feedback: This is a position because it answers the assignment with what the school should do. The topic is the weekly outdoor lunch day.

options.text: Students could use a relaxing break during the school day.
options.feedback: This is a possible reason for a position. The topic is the weekly outdoor lunch day at school.

questions.correct_explanation: A topic names the subject. A position answers the assignment question about that subject.

questions.prompt: Which sentence takes a position on the same assignment?

options.text: Outdoor lunch is a meal students eat outside.
options.feedback: This describes the topic but does not answer whether the school should offer outdoor lunch.

options.text: Students eat lunch at school each weekday.
options.feedback: This gives information about lunch, but it does not take a position on the assignment question.

options.text: Our school should offer an outdoor lunch day each week because it may give students a relaxing break.
options.feedback: Correct. The sentence answers the question with a position and gives a reason.

questions.correct_explanation: A position answers the question. A reason can point toward what the writer will explain, but it does not have to use this exact wording.

reflect.heading: Check your writing
reflect.instructions: Return to your Introduction in the editor. Read the assignment and your own writing. Choose the response that best describes your review; neither choice is scored by EssayScaff.

questions.prompt: Does my Introduction discuss the assignment question?

options.label: Yes, I have checked that it discusses the question.
I want to review or revise it.
Yes, I have checked that readers can find my position.
I want to review or revise it.

reflect.privacy_note: Your selection is a student self-check, not a machine-detected result. It stays in this browser session; EssayScaff does not detect or judge your answer.

completion_conditions: The student has viewed the Model step.
The student has answered each Practice question correctly; incorrect answers show an explanation and require retry before progressing.
The student has selected a response for both Reflect questions.
Completion means the student finished this lesson activity. It does not establish writing mastery and does not control access to Body or any other stage.
lesson_limitations: The sample assignment and example are fictional teaching examples written for this lesson.
The lesson is a brief introduction, not a full SRSD intervention or a substitute for teacher guidance.
Practice correctness refers only to recognizing the lesson's example topic and position; it says nothing about the student's essay quality.
